content.title: About
content.content: A milk shake is a home‑prepared beverage made from milk, cream, and fruit or berry purée. It can be light (about 150 kcal per 250 ml) and contains no chocolate, offering flavors such as vanilla, strawberry, mango, banana, and caramel.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Making it at home lets you control sugar and additive levels.
Seasonal fruits or spices like cinnamon can change the flavor profile.
The shake can be made vegan by substituting dairy with plant‑based milks.
Cold shakes retain more vitamins than hot drinks.
Texture depends on the milk‑to‑cream ratio; more cream yields a richer mouthfeel.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Milk provides calcium essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The shake supplies complete protein that supports muscle repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants (with berry flavors)
items.content: Berries such as strawberry or blueberry add vitamin C and polyphenols.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who are lactose intolerant may experience discomfort; lactose‑free milk is a suitable alternative.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey requires using plant‑based milk substitutes.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Adding excessive sugar or syrups raises calories and may contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Even a light shake can become calorie‑dense if too much cream or fruit juice is used.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Blend 200 ml milk, 50 ml cream, about 100 g of chosen fruit purée, and optional sweetener until smooth. Chill for 5–10 minutes and serve with fresh fruit slices or a sprig of mint.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed immediately. If needed, keep refrigerated in a sealed container for up to 24 hours; give it a quick stir before serving.
